symptom: Review of ako/mxcli#824 (#818): under mdl 1, `create or modify` that removed a parameter still acted on by `delete $Acc` (or commit/change/rollback/retrieve-over-association/loop) wrote the flow with the parameter gone and reported success — no check, no --references warning, CE error only at mx check. And an inserted run stating @position on a later statement but not the first lost the position and wrote the two new nodes on top of each other.
cause: SetHeader's usesVariable matched only `$Name` in strings, but most actions store the variable they act on bare (DeleteVariableName "Acc", CommitVariableName, ChangeVariableName, StartVariableName, IteratedListVariableName, …). Fragment placement keyed only on the FIRST statement's @position (MicroflowFragment.Placed); otherwise the whole fragment was translated into the gap, discarding a later stated position.
insight: A 'variable still used' check by text search must know both spellings Mendix stores a use in: `$Name` inside expressions and the bare name in *VariableName properties — excluding the declaring ones (VariableName, OutputVariableName, ResultVariableName, LoopVariableName), since a flow may legitimately declare a variable named after the removed parameter. Found by creating a param used only by `delete $P`, then removing it: the writer's claim 'refused if still used' was tested only with a log expression.
